text_plugin_synopsis: Photo capture, continuous frame analysis and viewfinder preview through CameraX, with frames ready for OCR, barcode, YOLO and other recognition modules

p_introduction_what: 3-Prism Camera is the camera plugin of AutoJs6. Built on Jetpack CameraX, it gives scripts photo capture, continuous frame analysis and viewfinder preview. Live frames reach the script as AutoJs6 `ImageWrapper` objects, so a script can hand them straight to existing modules such as `ocr`, `barcode` or `yolo` for live barcode scanning, text recognition and object detection.
p_introduction_how: The plugin owns the camera and talks to AutoJs6 over Binder: live frames travel through a shared memory ring buffer (temporary files on Android 7.0 - 8.0), photos reach AutoJs6 as JPEG to be decoded or saved unchanged, and the preview renders straight into a `SurfaceView` of the script's interface, so no pixels cross Binder. While a session is open, the plugin runs a camera foreground service, so scripts keep receiving frames in the background or with the screen off.
p_status_note: The camera core, the viewfinder and the settings page of 1.0.0 are done, and the release checks are in progress. The `camera` script module needs AutoJs6 {{ required_host_version_name }} (internal version {{ required_host_version_code }}) or later.
features: Photos: returns an `ImageWrapper` turned upright by its EXIF orientation, or saves the original JPEG (with EXIF) to a path you choose; flash mode, quality and resolution are configurable.

Live frames: RGBA frames at 640x480 by default (changeable on the settings page) and up to 1920x1080, turned upright to match the screen by default; when a script falls behind, frames are dropped and counted instead of piling up.
Preview: hand a `SurfaceView` from a ui script or a floating window to the session to show the viewfinder, alongside live frames and photo capture.
Controls: lens selection, resolution, target frame rate, torch, flash mode, zoom, exposure compensation and tap to focus, with readable ranges and current state.

Capture screen: opening the plugin from the launcher shows the capture screen, with lens switching, the flashlight, zoom and tap to focus; photos taken there are only shown, not saved, and the top right button opens the settings; `camera.capture({ ui: true })` opens the same screen, and the script gets the photo when the user presses the shutter, or `null` when the user cancels.

Works in the background: a camera foreground service runs while a session is open, so frames keep coming in the background or with the screen off; the camera is released when the script exits or AutoJs6 is stopped.
usage_steps: Download the APK that matches the device ABI from [Releases]({{ repo_url }}/releases) and install it: most phones need `arm64-v8a`; if unsure, choose `universal`, which works on every device but is larger.
Open the plugin and grant the camera permission when asked; scripts can also call `camera.requestPermission()` to open the permission screen.
To use the `camera` module in scripts, update AutoJs6 to build {{ required_host_version_code }} ({{ required_host_version_name }}) or later and enable this plugin in the Plugin Center.
p_usage_note: The plugin supports devices running Android {{ min_android_version }} (API {{ android_min_sdk }}) or later. There is one package per ABI and a `universal` package for every device; the few native libraries that come with CameraX and Compose (about 50 KB per ABI) are aligned to 16 KB memory pages, so newer devices with 16 KB pages install it as well.
compatibility_points: Android 7.0 (API 24) and later, with no ABI restriction: arm64-v8a, armeabi-v7a, x86_64 and x86 each have a package, and the `universal` package fits every device.
Android 7.0 - 8.0 (API 24 - 26) have no shared memory, so frames reach AutoJs6 through temporary files and live frames run at a lower frame rate than on newer systems.

The `camera` script module needs AutoJs6 {{ required_host_version_name }} (internal version {{ required_host_version_code }}) or later; older AutoJs6 versions lack the module, while the viewfinder of the plugin still opens from the launcher.
Some vendor systems (such as ColorOS) restrict the camera for background apps further; the roadmap appendix F records the results per device.
p_script_api_intro: Scripts use these features through the global module `camera` (also available as `$camera`); see [AutoJs6 documentation > Camera](https://docs.autojs6.com/#/camera) for the full reference
api_points: `camera.capture(options)` opens, captures and closes in one step; `camera.open(options)` opens an exclusive session whose object offers `preview`, `analyze`, `capture`, `torch`, `zoom`, `exposure`, `focusAt`, `state` and `close`.

Frame lifetime: the `img` of an `analyze` callback is valid only while the callback runs and is recycled as soon as it returns; to use it afterwards, call `img.clone()` and `recycle()` the copy yourself.
`camera.list()` lists the lenses with their resolutions, zoom and exposure ranges; `camera.capabilities()` returns the contract version, the feature list and the permission state.
One session at a time: a second `open` fails with `CAMERA_BUSY` and names the holder; the session closes when the script exits.

faq.q: Why is the camera a plugin rather than part of AutoJs6?
faq.a: The camera needs CameraX and the foreground service permissions. As a plugin, users who do not need the camera carry neither the size nor the permissions, and the plugin can be updated independently of AutoJs6.

faq.q: Can scripts receive frames in the background?
faq.a: Yes, as long as the session is opened while AutoJs6 is in the foreground. While a session is open, the plugin runs a camera foreground service and the notification shows that the camera is in use. When AutoJs6 is already in the background or the phone sits at the lock screen (Android 11 and later), the system does not allow camera use, and a session opened then reports CAMERA_DISABLED and closes. Some vendor systems restrict background cameras further; see the device matrix in the roadmap.

faq.q: Does the plugin save photos to the gallery?
faq.a: No. The plugin requests no storage permission and never writes to the system gallery; AutoJs6 writes a photo only to the `path` a script passes.

p_security_intro: The plugin keeps its permission surface as small as possible:
security_points: Protected entry points: the capability service and the activation entry require the AutoJs6 plugin permission (`org.autojs.permission.PLUGIN`), so other apps cannot call them; the foreground service and the transparent start screen are not exported.

Camera: only `CAMERA`, the camera foreground service permissions and, on Android 13 or later, the notification permission for the camera-in-use notification are requested; the camera is used only while a session is open and is released as soon as the session closes, the script exits or AutoJs6 is stopped.

Network and storage: the network permission serves only the update check of the settings page (it reads only the AutoJs6 official plugin index, automatic checks at most once every 12 hours, can be turned off), and no storage permission is requested; frames and photos pass only between the plugin and AutoJs6, are never uploaded and never reach the system gallery.
Exclusive use: one session at a time (a script or the plugin's capture screen), and the error message names the holder.
